messages.subject: R code Snippets
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,

    First I want to thank Stephan for the StatET plug-in.

    I can only have 8 R Snippets in the Object Browser and the rest of R
code Snippets that were set in preference were ignored.

   Is this a bug or I miss something?

How can I use this expression

"window" , snippet "View(${r_object_name})".

link:

http://comments.gmane.org/gmane.comp.ide.eclipse.statet/121


Version: Kepler Service Release 2
StatET: 3.3.2

Regards,

M. H. Ferdosi

messages.subject: Re: R code Snippets
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

[2014-06-16 09:32] mh fe wrote:
> Dear All,
>
>      First I want to thank Stephan for the StatET plug-in.
>
>      I can only have 8 R Snippets in the Object Browser and the rest of
> R code Snippets that were set in preference were ignored.
>
>     Is this a bug or I miss something?

There is no limit, also more snippets works for me. Note that the menu 
shows only snippets which are valid at the current context (selection); 
valid means, all variables of the snippet can be resolved.

>
> How can I use this expression
>
> "window" , snippet "View(${r_object_name})".

This should work e.g. for an selected element in the Object Browser or 
if the cursor is in an element name in the R editor.

Regards,
Stephan

messages.subject: content assist settings
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to set the content assist, to pop up directly when typing the $ key in the editor window and to show the column names of the corresponding data.frame in the "Default proposals" (which are shown first). This was the behaviour on my old XP machine with Eclipse 3.8.2 and StatET 3.2.0.b201302101630E38sw.

Now with eclipse 3.8.2 and StatET 3.3.2 on windows 7, the content assist is only shown after being invoked by CTRL+SPACE and the column names are only shown in the "All R Console Proposals", which means that the CTRL+SPACE have to be pressed 3 times succesively. Is it possible to change this?

Different settings in the R Console Content Assist Preferences have no effect.

Thanks and regards,
Marco
